facts.value: Islam is a monotheistic religion based on the Quran, considered by Muslims to be revealed by God, and on the teachings (hadith) of the Islamic prophet Muhammad.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Islam is based on the unity of all religious philosophies and accepts all of the Abrahamic prophets of Judaism, Christianity and other Abrahamic religions before Muhammad.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Islam is the most widely practiced religion of Southeast Asia, North Africa, Western Asia, and Central Asia, and also exists in parts of South Asia, Sub-Saharan Africa, and Southeast Europe.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: There are about 1.8 billion followers of Islam, which is almost a quarter of the earth's population.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Sunni Islam is the largest denomination within Islam and follows the Qur'an and the ahadith.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Shia Islam is the second largest denomination of Islam and its adherents believe that Ali succeeded Muhammad.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: There are various Muslim revivalist movements such as Muwahhidism and Salafism.
facts.programme_association: Online Bachelor of Arts in Religious Studies – Religion, Culture and Public Life

facts.value: Other denominations of Islam include Nation of Islam, Ibadi, Sufism, Quranism, Mahdavia, Ahmadiyya and non-denominational Muslims.

facts.value: Wahhabism is the dominant Muslim school of thought in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
